text: A melted chocolate bar invented the microwave oven. Nineteen forty-five. Engineer Percy Spencer is standing next to a radar tube called a magnetron. The chocolate bar in his pocket melts. Nothing touched it. So he tries popcorn. It pops. Then an egg. It explodes in a colleague's face. Microwaves flip water molecules back and forth, two point four five billion times a second. That shaking is heat. The first microwave oven was taller than a man and weighed three hundred and forty kilos. And microwaves only reach a few centimetres into food. That's why the middle is still frozen.
